brief: THE BET — rung 4b. Put an EYOT in the river: a small island in the river's EAST half (the boat's channel is x 116.5–121.5 and must stay clear; the deck is rows 30–32 and the lane bridge 64–66, so site it between, roughly x 122.5–126 × y 40–52, or wherever your own read of the water says), with a shingle bank, reeds at its edges and ONE willow whose fronds hang over the water and lean with windDir(). It is land: WATER cells become a new tile (EYOT or BANK — add it to buildGrid(), the census TN list and groundCol), the swans' SWAN_BANK logic gets a third bank, the river streaks in drawRiverFlow part around it, and ducks nest on it in spring (a seasonal thing on it, priced with a probe, is welcome). The census MUST move — water down, tileKinds +1, speciesKinds +1 if the willow is a new species — re-pin the baseline and say so. A 150–300-line diff is expected and welcome: this is the first landform the river has ever had and it is in the centre of every wide shot.
successLooksLike: From the wide shot at noon the river has an island with a willow on it; the rowboat passes it on the west; a swan preens against its bank; at 3x on the Far bank quarter the reeds and the willow's fronds are legible; naming says 'the eyot' / 'the willow on the eyot'; the census shows water reduced by the footprint and a new tile kind.
avoid: Do not put it under the deck or the lane bridge, and do not narrow the boat's channel — trace one boat spawn → despawn on ten seeds and show 0 boat frames inside the footprint. Do not route walkers onto it (no waypoint set may name it — the waypoints law). Do not add a second R() draw per frame for the fronds: hash per frond.
